raw_response:
I farm only 8.2 mu, so I cannot spread money everywhere. I still do what has kept the family steady for years: wheat and maize on the main land, and a smaller piece of cotton for cash. I do not like making big changes. If I cut fertilizer too much and the crop goes weak, that loss hurts more than saving a little money. But I also cannot buy too much at once, because people in the house work outside and cash must be kept in hand.

For wheat, I will keep the better land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, about 5.2 mu. Wheat is our steady crop. I will sow in early October, like most people here, using the common local seed I can buy in town. I will put base fertilizer before sowing, then watch the color of the wheat in spring. If it looks yellow at jointing, I will topdress again. Water from the well costs money, so I will not water blindly, but wheat still needs two or three turns if rain is short. After wheat harvest in June, there is no time to waste. I will clear the field quickly and plant maize right away, same land, no deep tillage, mostly quick rotary tillage or direct seeding after harvest. Maize grows fast here if you catch the moisture, so I would rather plant quickly than make the field look perfect.

Cotton I will keep on about 3 mu. Cotton takes more hand work, but it brings cash if the year is decent, so I do not want to give it up fully. I will not put the best money into cotton because picking and pest control cost more, and family labor is not always at home. I will use a moderate amount of fertilizer, irrigate when it is really dry, and spray only when I see insects or disease pressure. This year my thinking is simple: keep the wheat-maize land stable, keep some cotton for income, spend carefully, and use the well when the crop truly needs it.
